Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-09-01 | AAPL | Overweight | -3.0% | -3.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, but build it on the pullback, not at the 325.13 close — do not add inside the 322–327 chop zone while price sits $2.74 above the upper Bollinger band (322.39) after a +7.6%/13-session run. Cap the position at ~1.0x a standard AAPL allocation until FQ4 confirms gross margin ≥49% and the raw-materials build converts, with the 1.25x upgrade reserved for a close above 344.57 or that fundamental proof. Tranche 1 only: 25% of target weight at 316.00 (10 EMA 315.79) and a further 15% into 311.30–313.00 (Bollinger mid 311.32 / VWMA 312.49 / 50 SMA 312.94) on stabilization, sized off a gap to 295.00 at a 0.5–0.75% equity loss rather than off the 305.00 closing stop; Tranche 2 (20–25%) only on a close above 327.30 with ≥42M shares, preferably 50M+ or a second consecutive above-average session. Trim 10–15% into 333.43–335.00 if that supply zone rejects, trail the rest under the 10 EMA, halt all buying on a close below 311.30 and exit on a close below 300.00.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats agreed on direction and fought only over sizing and entry — so the rating is directionally settled and the work is in the mechanics. Overweight is the right expression; Buy at spot is not, and the conservative's event-driven wait is not.

What the bull won outright and nobody rebutted: the operating record. Revenue +16.2% to $364.36B, gross margin 49.07% with FQ3 at 50.06% (still expanding sequentially into June), operating income +21.7%, diluted EPS +22.4%, operating cash flow +43.1%, free cash flow +52.5% to $110.2B, net cash up $28.5B to $62.22B, $14.4B of gross debt retired with zero new long-term issuance. The quality-of-earnings item the conservative never touched is the strongest single fact in the file: accounts receivable fell ~21% while revenue grew ~16%, and finished goods inventory declined — cash-backed growth, not channel stuffing. The tape corroborates: 325.13 is above the 10 EMA (315.79), the 50 SMA (312.94) and a 200 SMA that rose every session in the sample; the MACD histogram is positive and expanding five sessions running; VWMA curled from 307.76 (8/19) to 312.49; the breakout bar printed 53.17M shares against a ~41.9M twenty-one-day average (+27%) with RSI 61 — headroom, not overbought. My own record is explicit on the cost of fighting this: the 2026-08-25 Hold (+5.5% five-day alpha forfeited), the 08-24, 08-21 and 08-20 Underweights (+1.6%, +2.9%, −0.1% alpha) and the July Underweight string all lost relative return by treating momentum decay or a compressed coil as a reason to under-own an intact primary trend. That is why this is not Hold and not Underweight.

What the bears won, and why it is not Buy: spot asymmetry. From 325.13, the first gap target at 333.43 is +2.6% against −4.3% to the 311.30 confluence and −7.7% to 300. The conservative's forensic counters also land: opex grew +21.9% against gross profit +21.7%, so there is no operating leverage — the entire operating-margin gain came off the gross-margin line, and there is no segment or mix data in this run to prove 49–50% is a structural shift rather than favorable timing ahead of a memory-cost reset. The $13.3B intangible addition matched by a $13.5B rise in other noncurrent liabilities remains unexplained (an AI asset on the bull's inference, a deferred payment obligation on the bear's — neither proven). The effective tax rate is worsening (FQ3 17.86% vs 9M 17.58%), buybacks fell 12% to $62.1B so the mechanical EPS tailwind is fading, and the bull's "late-October re-acceleration" is hope rather than data.

The decision between the seats is on sizing, and the neutral seat plus the conservative's gap arithmetic carried it. The conservative is right that a 1% budget measured on 316→305 becomes ~1.9% of equity on a repeat of the 7/31 gap (333.43→304.81, −8.6%, 132.5M shares), with 6/25 (−6.1%, 107M) as corroboration — ATR 7.63 means a 305 stop is less than half an ATR away and can be jumped. So the share count is sized off gap slippage to 295.00 at 0.5–0.75% of equity, not off the closing stop; the stop stays at 305.00 closing basis only as the normal-drift invalidation. But the conservative overreaches in two places and loses those: waiting for FQ4 gross margin ≥49% and inventory conversion *before any build* is no longer a staged buy, it forfeits the defined 311.30–316.00 confluence, and it is precisely the over-strict confirmation stack my 08-25 reflection identified as the error that cost +5.5% of alpha; and pre-positioning 40% at 316.00 without a gap-adjusted budget, as the aggressive seat wants, is the mirror-image mistake — his 1.6:1 first-target payoff becomes less than 1:1 on gap stress. The neutral construction survives: cap at 1.0x standard until FQ4, split tranche 1 into 25% at 316.00 plus 15% at 311.30–313.00 on stabilization, require ≥42M (preferably 50M+ or a second above-average session) on the 327.30 close before Tranche 2 at 20–25%, and do not hold the retained third blindly through the September product event and FQ4 — trim 10–15% into 333.43–335.00 if that zone rejects and trail under the 10 EMA. The aggressive seat's dismissal of the Ternus handover, the Schiller App Store reshuffle and the OpenAI trade-secret suit as pure narrative is directionally fair (pre-announced, no damages figure, no injunction) but the coverage is admittedly incomplete, which is additional reason to hold less than 1.25x into the event rather than more.

Catalysts and gaps. Late-October FQ4 FY26: gross margin ≥49% (memory-cost pass-through), raw-materials conversion without a reserve charge, the FQ4 tax rate against the 17.86% FQ3 print, buyback re-authorization, and any 10-Q note explaining the $13.3B intangible and the matching $13.5B liability. What would change the call: upgrade to 1.25x/Buy on a decisive close above the 333.43–344.57 gap/supply zone or on FQ4 gross margin ≥49% with the intangible reconciled; downgrade to Underweight on a close below 311.30 (cut back to Tranche 1 and re-underwrite), on an FQ4 guide below 48.5%, or on a close under 300.00, which exits and reopens the June low at 275.15. Stated gaps, not papered over: no sentiment report, no insider-transaction data, no valuation/consensus or segment/mix disclosure, and no options chain or implied-vol data in this run — so the margin-durability and AI-monetization questions are genuinely open, a protective collar or put cannot be priced here, and all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL weight with tech-only targets, not valuation-derived ones.

**Price Target**: 333.43

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -3.1% (raw -3.0%) says the Overweight direction was wrong out of the gate, though five sessions is far too short to judge a call written to the late-October FQ4 print. What this window undercuts is the tape corroboration — the "MACD expanding five sessions, above the 10 EMA" argument decayed immediately, with price sliding from 325.13 back into the 311.30–316.00 confluence — while the operating-quality evidence is simply untested; the tactical caution against buying at spot was right, but it was right for the wrong reason, since the pullback arrived as trend weakness rather than as a discount. The lesson: with ATR 7.63 (~2.3% of spot), a Tranche 1 placed only 2.8% below the close fills inside the first week of noise, so stage entries at least one ATR apart and halve the first tranche rather than treating a fast fill as a gift.

[2026-08-31 | AAPL | Overweight | -0.2% | -0.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL — constructive, but not at the mid-range price. Build toward 120% of a standard single-name allocation in tranches, starting with a deliberately small first tranche: 5% of standard (not the trader's 10%) via GTC limits at 312–314, never chasing above 318. Do not use 308.80 as the stop — it is 0.58 ATR in a name whose August 31 range alone was 8.44 points; use a hard stop at 305.70 (one ATR below entry), treat a daily close below the 50-SMA at 312.38 as the de-risk warning, and cap total tactical risk at 0.75% of portfolio until the 10-Q business-combination/other-noncurrent-liability notes are read and the late-October FQ4 gross margin confirms the inventory build was demand-driven. Add only on a daily close above 322.37 on ≥60M shares; take partial profit at 326.79 and treat 333.43–334.99 as a stretch target. Invalidate the Overweight stance on a close below the rising 200-SMA at 282.81. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not the contested question; the entry geometry is, and that is what fixes the rating at Overweight rather than Buy.

What the bulls won, unopposed. No seat disputed the operating record: FQ3 revenue +16.4%, gross margin 50.06% with 71.9% incremental gross margin, diluted EPS +28.7%, operating cash flow +43.1%, free cash flow +52.5%, net cash nearly doubled to $62.2B, debt/equity 0.78x and the current ratio above 1.0x for the first time. None of that is consistent with a broken franchise, and the conservative seat conceded as much: "the 200-SMA at 282.81 is rising and AAPL is 12% above it, the 50/200 spread is widening, and the fundamentals… support owning this name. I have no argument with the direction." The primary trend corroborates the business: AAPL at 316.85 is +12% above a rising 200-SMA, has held the 50-SMA at 312.38 for four consecutive sessions (313.45, 314.58, 319.70, 316.85), the 10-EMA at 313.71 has inflected up from 308.76 on 08-17, and the 50/200 spread has widened from 13.8 points on June 2 to 29.6 points. MACD crossed its signal on 08-26 with the histogram expanding monotonically +0.152 → +0.416 → +0.896 → +0.977 and crossed zero at +0.297 from a −2.676 trough on 08-17; RSI 54.08 and MFI 57.2 leave room; VWMA 310.80 is turning up with price 1.95% above it. My own record makes the same point: the 08-21 (+2.9% alpha) and 08-24 (+1.6%) AAPL Underweights both lost five-day alpha, and the 08-24 reflection codified the fix — do not trim a compressed range only ~3% above a four-times-tested floor on momentum decay alone, and require a volume-confirmed close below the trigger before acting. A short into this structure, against $62.2B of net cash and a 50% gross margin, is a range trade, not an investment call.

What the bears won, and why it is not a Buy at 316.85. The conservative's arithmetic on the stop is the single best piece of analysis in the debate and the aggressive seat never answered it. A 4.2-point stop from 313 is 0.58 ATR at an ATR of 7.245 (2.29% of price); the August 31 session alone ranged 312.80–321.24, 8.44 points. A stop inside half a normal daily range is a wager on the noise distribution, so the aggressive seat cannot simultaneously call 308.80 "structural" and ignore that an ordinary macro dip books a loss before the thesis is tested. The neutral framed the correction correctly: the fix is not to abandon the trade but to halve the tranche and widen the stop to roughly one ATR, keeping dollar risk constant while cutting the probability of a noise stop-out. Second, the tape is a range, not a confirmed trend: three consecutive rejections into 320–322 (322.37 on 08-28, 321.24 on 08-31, closing 316.85 in the lower half of the day's range), an unfilled 304.81–333.43 crash-candle gap overhead, and light participation — August 31 printed 41.24M against a ~43M August norm, while the period's largest volume prints were all down sessions (107.0M on 06-25, 132.5M on 07-31, 261.8M on 06-26). The aggressive seat's claim that volume is "lagging" is wrong; it is coincident evidence of participation, and the neutral's reading — upside provisional, volume therefore governs the add, not the probe — is the correct one. Third, unresolved event and disclosure risk: the Ternus handoff on September 1 (announcement priced, strategy not), a possible September rate hike plus the jobs print and Broadcom's AI earnings inside the same window, inventory +94% with raw materials +260% and 61.6 days of COGS versus 34.0 at fiscal year-end, deferred revenue +8.8% against revenue +16.2% (tilting the margin expansion toward cyclical hardware pricing and component tailwinds rather than services mix), and a $13.3B intangible build matched by +$13.5B of other noncurrent liabilities with no 10-Q note in the evidence set. A stop controls price; it does not control a gap on a note disclosure. Finally, valuation: ~35–39x run-rate EPS on ~$8.73–8.75 TTM EPS gives no cushion if FQ4 gross margin breaks.

Where each seat overreached. The aggressive seat is right that the conservative's two-outcome menu (a 60M close above 322.37, or a flush to 302–305 with a stop below 295) risks never getting filled — AAPL can grind sideways in the 312–316 shelf for a week — and the neutral's verdict that a small, wider-stopped probe beats both a chase and a freeze is the winning construction. But the aggressive seat's 4.9R framing answers "how much if I'm right," not expectancy, and its treatment of the CEO handoff as a free positive catalyst and of the $13.3B intangible as resolved by two line items matching in magnitude are unverified assumptions doing real work. The conservative seat is right on stop geometry, on the volume read, and on the case for halving size and capping tactical risk at 0.75%; it overreaches only in requiring a 60M-share up-day or a deep flush before any exposure at all, which converts staged accumulation into momentum chasing. The neutral seat's synthesis carries the day: keep the long bias, cut the first tranche to ~5% of standard, widen the stop to ~305.70, de-risk on a close below 312.38 rather than standing aside only below 308.80, hold the add at a 322.37 close on ≥60M, take partial profit at 326.79 and demote 333.43–334.99 to a stretch target.

Why not Buy, and why not Hold. Buy would require the trader's full 10% first tranche at 313 on a 0.58-ATR stop into a September 1 handoff, a jobs report, an unresolved potential rate hike and an unread 10-Q note — two of three risk seats explicitly rejected that geometry and neither was rebutted on the arithmetic. Hold would ignore a live, widening 50/200 structure, a fresh MACD zero-cross, and a franchise generating $110B+ of nine-month FCF; it also repeats the error the 08-24 reflection named, of failing to carry constructive exposure inside an intact primary trend. Overweight — real but staged and smaller than the trader proposed — is the honest size of the edge.

What would change the rating. Upgrade toward Buy on a daily close above 333.43 on sustained volume expansion with MACD holding positive and an FQ4 gross margin ≥49.5% with inventory flat-to-down; a close above 322.37 on ≥60M shares is the interim trigger that unlocks the second tranche (targets 326.79, then the 333.43–334.99 gap). Downgrade toward Underweight on a daily close below 308.80 on above-average volume (then 300.00, then the 282.81 200-SMA, which would invalidate the primary trend outright), on FQ4 gross margin below 49% with rising inventory, or if the 10-K shows the $13.3B intangible carries amortization or impairment risk. Stated gaps, not papered over: no sentiment or positioning report was supplied (missing data is a gap, not a neutral signal); no options chain or implied-volatility data, so the neutral's premium-selling overlay and any collar cannot be priced here; news coverage is partial, so the cause of the 07-31 −7.35%/132.5M-share gap remains unestablished; no consensus forward EPS or valuation multiple to verify the 35–39x figure; and no portfolio context, so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL weight and every listed level is technical rather than valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 326.79

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 print

REFLECTION:
Five days produced −0.2% raw and −0.1% alpha versus SPY, which is effectively flat and far too short a window to adjudicate a 1–3 month Overweight thesis — this is noise, not a verdict. The near-zero alpha does mildly undercut the premise that the 312–316 shelf would resolve upward promptly, but it equally reflects the deliberately tiny 5% first tranche, so the constructive structural read (rising 200-SMA, widening 50/200 spread) is neither supported nor broken. The concrete lesson: for staged-entry calls, measure performance from the actual fill and hold the sizing decision accountable, because a 5% probe against a 1–3 month horizon will read as zero alpha regardless of whether the thesis is right.
